thread.title: Brace for a sudden, sharp rally for the S&P 500 in 2019, says strategist David Bianco

author: kopitiambot.com
title: Brace for a sudden, sharp rally for the S&P 500 in 2019, says strategist David Bianco
text:
(Source: marketwatch.com )
Welcome to the day that could make investors’ Christmas merry and bright or deliver one final crushing blow to hope for a Santa rally.
A little optimism is peeking through as investors watch for one of the biggest Fed decisions in years. “Jerome Powell is damned if he does and damned if doesn’t on Wednesday,” the anonymous blogger for The Heisenberg Report summed up nicely.
Poll: What will Fed do on Wednesday and what will the market reaction be?
— Ramp Capital ♿️ (@RampCapitalLLC) December 18, 2018
And even if Powell tosses this market a bone with some dovish talk or even backs off a rate increase, wariness abounds for 2019, with the so-called smart-money crowd maintaining an apparently bearish stance .
Our call of the day gives investors 12 reasons to be bullish — and they’ll need it. It comes from Deutsche Bank’s former chief U.S. equity analyst David Bianco, who last week predicted a 5% to 10% rally in the next month or so.
Brace for the S&P 500 to surge “suddenly and sharply,” says Bianco, now chief investment strategist at DWS, as he believes “now is one of the best entry points into U.S. equities.”
“Too many investors are missing the big picture in our view,” he says. “The known challenges and risks facing the global economy and equities are muted relative to the uncertainties during 2009-2016.” He sees the S&P 500 at 2,950 by the end of 2019.
Since Bianco’s note pubbed on Dec. 14, the S&P has had two very ugly sessions and a pretty muted one Wednesday, but anyway here are his 12 bullish reasons:
1) Economic expansion will go on through 2020
2) Previously a “top bear growl,” U.S. households in pretty good financial shape
3) Corporate, bank balance sheets strong
4) U.S. corporate tax cut amounts to “important structural incentive change,” will probably never go back to 35%
5) Capital expenditure should keep rising, industries that look for and support secular growth opportunities tend to do better in the latter part of an economic cycle.
6) Inflation, interest rates still low vs. history
7) Current interest rates suggest S&P 500 price/earnings ratio of 20 is fair.
8) Fund investment fees are low vs. history
9) Dollar, oil prices won’t trigger S&P 500 profit recession
10) Federal debt to GDP is manageable
11) China growth will slow, but it’s still huge and a boost to GDP
12) Europe will survive and the U.K. will get a last-ditch soft Brexit deal
So stuff that in your stocking. Ho, ho, let’s go.

The chart So, share repurchases soared 58% in the third quarter, the third straight record as companies put corporate tax savings to work. Our chart of the day from Wolf Street’s Wolf Richter looks at the quarter’s No. 2 buyback queen (Qualcomm
QCOM, +0.03%
was No. 1)—Apple
AAPL, +0.21%
which he notes spent over $700 billion in 2018 on buybacks, and as shares tanked the latter part of this year.
“This is the vengeance of share buybacks. They accomplish absolutely nothing. But they waste huge amounts of money,” says Richter. He says Apple could have been inventing new things and building U.S. plants with that money and its market value has plunged nearly 30% since Oct. 3, he notes.
Note, the Bank of America Merrill Lynch fund manager found that for the first time since 2008/09, investors want companies to start improving balance sheets with far fewer asking for buybacks.
